title: Merge Operations to Turn Array Into a Palindrome
summary: Given an array of positive integers, you can repeatedly combine adjacent elements into their sum.
statement: Given an array of positive integers, you can repeatedly combine adjacent elements into their sum. Determine the least number of such operations required to transform the array into a palindrome.
constraints: One operation replaces two adjacent elements by their sum.
Return the minimum operations needed to make the resulting array a palindrome.
reference_solution:
def minimum_merges_to_palindrome(nums):
    left=0;right=len(nums)-1;left_sum=nums[left];right_sum=nums[right];operations=0
    while left<right:
        if left_sum==right_sum:left+=1;right-=1
        elif left_sum<right_sum:left+=1;left_sum+=nums[left];operations+=1;continue
        else:right-=1;right_sum+=nums[right];operations+=1;continue
        if left<right:left_sum=nums[left];right_sum=nums[right]
    return operations

hints: Compare accumulated values from the two ends.
Equal end sums can be fixed as matching palindrome entries and both pointers advance inward.
When unequal, merge the smaller side with its next inner value and count one operation.
Positive values mean only growing the smaller side can reach equality without wasting a necessary merge, so the greedy choices are forced.

tests.explanation: Merging the leading four with three and later balancing the opposite side yields a palindrome in two operations.
Three merges are required because no smaller sequence of adjacent sums can balance both ends.
